title: Double transpose of tensor-counit maps for composite adjunctions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y,\mathcal C_Z$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category], and let $S_f:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$ and $S_g:\mathcal C_Z\to\mathcal C_Y$ be strong monoidal functors [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Let $P_f:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$ and $P_g:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_Z$ have right adjoints $G_f,G_g$, with specified adjunction Hom bijections and counits $\epsilon_f:P_fG_f\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\epsilon_g:P_gG_g\to\mathrm{id}$. Use their composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Suppose $P_f$ has a projection formula relative to $S_f$ and $P_g$ one relative to $S_g$, meaning natural isomorphisms with the unit and associativity equations of [def-sfb-projection-formula], written
$$\pi^f_{B,M}:P_f(S_fB\otimes M)\xrightarrow{\sim}B\otimes P_fM,\qquad
\pi^g_{K,L}:P_g(S_gK\otimes L)\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes P_gL.$$
All following expressions use the specified associators, unitors and strong monoidal comparisons. Give $P_c=P_gP_f$ relative to $S_c=S_fS_g$ the composite projection isomorphism
$$\pi^c_{K,M}=\pi^g_{K,P_fM}\circ P_g(\pi^f_{S_gK,M}),$$
and put $G_c=G_fG_g$, with counit $\epsilon^c_K=\epsilon_{g,K}\circ P_g(\epsilon_{f,G_gK})$.
For $h=f,g,c$ define $W_h=G_h\mathbf1$ and $\tau^h_B:S_hB\otimes W_h\to G_hB$ as the adjoint transpose of
$$P_h(S_hB\otimes W_h)\xrightarrow{\pi^h_{B,W_h}}B\otimes P_hW_h
\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{h,\mathbf1}}B\otimes\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\rho_B}B.$$
Write $W=W_f$, $V=W_g$, and $q=\tau^f_V:S_fV\otimes W\to G_fV=W_c$. For any $K\in\mathcal C_Z$ let $N=S_f(S_gK\otimes V)\otimes W$, identified with $S_cK\otimes S_fV\otimes W$. Under
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_X}(N,G_fG_gK)\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_Z}(P_gP_fN,K),$$
both morphisms
$$\tau^f_{G_gK}\circ(S_f\tau^g_K\otimes1_W),\qquad
\tau^c_K\circ(1_{S_cK}\otimes q)$$
have the same inverse transpose, namely
$$\begin{aligned}
P_gP_fN&\xrightarrow{P_g\pi^f_{S_gK\otimes V,W}}
P_g((S_gK\otimes V)\otimes P_fW)\\
&\xrightarrow{P_g(1\otimes\epsilon_{f,\mathbf1})}P_g(S_gK\otimes V)
\xrightarrow{\pi^g_{K,V}}K\otimes P_gV
\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{g,\mathbf1}}K.
\end{aligned}$$
The unit constraints are inserted in the last and second arrows. No $\tau^h$, $q$ or $W_h$ is assumed invertible, and no geometric morphism, smoothness or purity assertion is part of this statement.
The same formula holds for functors and adjunction Hom bijections restricted to full domains of definition, provided all the displayed objects, arrows, Hom bijections and the naturality and projection-coherence equations used in the two composites are defined and hold on those domains. No value outside these domains is asserted.

proof.text: For each $h∈\{f,g,c\}$, the definition of $\tau^h_B$ says that its inverse adjunction transpose is the composite $P_h(S_hB\otimes W_h)\xrightarrow{\pi^h_{B,W_h}}B\otimes P_hW_h\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{h,\mathbf1}}B\otimes\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\rho_B}B$. This is exactly the defining Hom-bijection equation, with the displayed associators and unitors included.

source.place: Second paragraph, sentence on transposing the two tensor transformations; adjunction transpose convention from Stacks Tag 0037.

proof.text: Transpose $\tau^f_{G_gK}\circ(S_f\tau^g_K\otimes1_W)$ successively through the composite Hom-bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. First transpose the outer $\tau^f$: by the defining equation in Step 1 this inserts $\pi^f_{S_gK\otimes V,W}$, then $1\otimes\epsilon_{f,\mathbf1}$, and then the right unitor. The remaining $\tau^g_K$ transposes in the same way, inserting $\pi^g_{K,V}$ and $1\otimes\epsilon_{g,\mathbf1}$. Naturality of the projection families and the associativity/unit coherence equations in [def-sfb-projection-formula] move the comparison maps through the tensor factors, so the resulting composite is precisely\n$$P_gP_fN\xrightarrow{P_g\pi^f_{S_gK\otimes V,W}}P_g((S_gK\otimes V)\otimes P_fW)\xrightarrow{P_g(1\otimes\epsilon_{f,\mathbf1})}P_g(S_gK\otimes V)\xrightarrow{\pi^g_{K,V}}K\otimes P_gV\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{g,\mathbf1}}K,$$\nwith the stated unit constraints.

source.place: Second paragraph, sentence on transposing the two tensor transformations and composing the two counits in adjunction order.

proof.text: For $\tau^c_K\circ(1_{S_cK}\otimes q)$, use $q=\tau^f_V$ and transpose through the composite adjunction. The defining equation for $\tau^c_K$ gives the composite projection $\pi^c_{K,M}=\pi^g_{K,P_fM}\circ P_g(\pi^f_{S_gK,M})$, while the composite counit is $\epsilon^c_K=\epsilon_{g,K}\circ P_g(\epsilon_{f,G_gK})$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Substituting $M=W$ and then the defining transpose equation for $q$ produces the same four-arrow composite displayed in Step 2; the associativity and unit constraints are exactly those stipulated in [def-sfb-projection-formula].

source.place: Second paragraph, sentence on the same projection formula and the same two counits in their adjunction order.

proof.text: The inverse transpose for the composite Hom-bijection is injective. Steps 2 and 3 show that the two displayed morphisms have the same inverse transpose, namely the displayed composite from $P_gP_fN$ to $K$; therefore the two morphisms are equal. No invertibility of $W_h$, $q$, or any $\tau^h$ is used, and the same argument applies after restricting to any full domains on which the stated adjunctions, projection maps, and coherence equations are defined.
